approved: Criminal Code Amendment (National Sport Integrity Offences) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create seven new federal crimes targeting match-fixing and similar actions that harm sport integrity.

The offences would be added as a new part of the Criminal Code, covering acts like corrupting a sporting event, offering or asking for bribes to influence a match, and hiding evidence of such corruption.
The government says the bill implements recommendations from the 2017 Wood Review, which found that inconsistent state laws leave sport vulnerable to match-fixing and organised crime.
Creates an offence of intentionally corrupting a sporting event to gain a benefit or cause a detriment.
Creates an offence of providing a benefit to someone, knowing it may lead them to corrupt a sporting event.
Creates an offence of asking for or accepting a benefit that may lead to corrupting a sporting event.
Creates an offence of altering, destroying or hiding information about corrupt conduct.
Makes the offences apply across national borders.
Links match-fixing offences to betting outcomes, even if the bet itself is lawful.
People involved in Australian sport, including athletes, officials, betting operators and spectators, as well as law enforcement agencies.

Introducing the Criminal Code Amendment (National Sport Integrity Offences) Bill 2026, the Minister said it creates national match-fixing offences carrying up to 10 years' imprisonment, implementing a 2017 review recommendation that Australia join the Macolin Convention against sports competition manipulation. She said sport generates $83 billion in combined economic, health and educational benefits annually, and the reforms aim to protect the integrity of Australian sport ahead of the 2032 Brisbane Olympic and Paralympic Games.

On behalf of Senator Sheldon, presented the Selection of Bills Committee's report recommending referral of the Commonwealth Land (Affordable Housing) Bill, the Crimes Amendment (Prohibiting Shackling During Childbirth) Bill and the Criminal Code Amendment (National Sport Integrity Offences) Bill to Senate committees for inquiry, alongside further amendments referring the Fair Super for Young Workers Bill and a bill on strip-searching of children.
